description: We are a team passionate about innovation, creativity, and teamwork. We enjoy exploring new ideas, challenging ourselves, and finding creative ways to solve problems. Our goal is not only to create something innovative and meaningful but also to have fun, learn from each other, and enjoy every step of the journey. We believe that great ideas come from working together, thinking outside the box, and having a positive attitude.
summary:
For our project, we chose the "Abandoned, but Not Forgotten" challenge, which involves creating an informative and engaging illustrated story or video for children and teenagers about the robotic missions and spacecraft left behind on the Moon over the decades.
We decided to create a short, three-page black-and-white comic. The story follows an astronaut who is sent on a special mission to investigate the Apollo 11 lunar module, The Eagle. Upon arriving on the Moon, the astronaut finds the spacecraft, and the two quickly befriend each other. Apollo 11 shares its incredible history—what it accomplished during its mission, how it operated, and how it ultimately became stranded and left behind on the lunar surface. When it is time to say goodbye, the astronaut returns to Earth carrying this knowledge so that everyone can learn its story.
We have already begun the brainstorming process and are currently working on storyboards and sketches in various styles to bring this adventure to life.
details: Our project aims to show future generations how humans managed to reach the Moon and return safely to Earth. By doing so, we hope to help children learn more about history and spark their interest in space and what lies beyond—perhaps even inspiring some to become scientists or astronauts in the future. We have used a comic-book style to illustrate a short story about the Apollo 11 mission, highlighting its objectives and the challenges it faced.
projectRefs: Apolo 11, a 50 años del hombre en la Luna
